project.description_en: At the end of the theme, the child presents a model farm with animals, says which animals are farmed and what they give us, imitates animal sounds in a story and explains why we must not throw rubbish in rivers.

activities.goal_en: Listen to a story and make the sounds of the animal characters.
activities.prompt_en: Listen to the story. When you hear an animal, make its sound!
steps_en: Tell the story slowly.
Stop at each animal so that the child makes its sound.
Ask: which animal woke up first?
Act the story in groups.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 33 (Storytelling: Sounds of animal characters), p. 60; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.story_en: Early in the morning, the cock said: “Cock-a-doodle-doo!” The goat woke up: “Meh, meh!” The cow mooed: “Moo!” The dog barked: “Woof, woof!” But the little pig was still sleeping. All the animals called together, very loudly. The little pig opened one eye and said: “Oink! Is it already morning?” And everybody laughed.

activities.goal_en: Mime animal behaviour and movement without speaking.
activities.prompt_en: Without a sound, move like an animal. Your friends guess which one!
steps_en: Mime an animal yourself (a snake, a bird, a tortoise).
The child guesses.
The child mimes an animal from a card.
Talk about how each animal moves.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 35 (Sign Language and Gestures: Mimes and mimics), p. 62; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Curly caterpillar letters: c, a, d, e, g, o
activities.goal_en: Write round letters that start like a c, turning anticlockwise.
activities.prompt_en: Like a curly caterpillar, these letters start with a c: c, a, d, o, g, e.
steps_en: Draw a c in the air, turning the right way.
Show how a, d, o and g start with c.
Trace them in sand.
Write a row of each.
observe_en: Starts each letter like a c.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 37 (Writing: Pre-letter formation), p. 64; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Recite a short French rhyme about farm animals.
activities.prompt_en: A little rhyme in French: “Cocorico, dit le coq. Meuh, dit la vache. Coin-coin, dit le canard.”
steps_en: Say the rhyme with the animal sounds.
The child repeats line by line.
Say it together with gestures.
Ask: what is “le coq”? (the cock)
observe_en: Gives the English for one animal.
materials_en: pictures of a cock, a cow, a duck
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 38 (French: Poésie et comptines), p. 65; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Sort animals into a set and find subsets.
activities.prompt_en: All these are animals. In this set, let us find a smaller group: the birds.
steps_en: Put animal pictures in a big circle (the set).
Find the birds and put them in a small circle inside (a subset).
Count the animals in the set and in the subset.
Find another subset: animals with four legs.
observe_en: Puts all the animals in the set.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 39 (Mathematics: Classifying sets and subsets), p. 66–67; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

interactive.prompt_en: In the set there are 9 animals. 3 are birds. How many are not birds?
interactive.explanation_en: Take away the 3 birds from 9 animals: 6 animals are not birds.

activities.title_en: Farm animals and what they give
activities.prompt_en: Farmers rear hens for eggs, cows for milk, fish in ponds, pigs, rabbits and snails.
steps_en: Show pictures of a poultry farm, a fish pond, a piggery, a rabbit hutch, snails.
Name each farm and what it gives.
Visit a farm or a hen house nearby if possible.
Make a model farm with clay animals.
observe_en: Says how farmers care for them.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 43 (Agriculture: Agricultural activities), p. 76; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Birds and insects in our compound
activities.goal_en: Observe nature and identify living things.
activities.prompt_en: Let us walk round the compound and look for birds and insects. We look, we do not catch.
steps_en: Walk quietly round the compound.
Look for birds, ants, butterflies, bees.
Count and draw what you see.
Talk: living things eat, grow and move.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 42 (Science and Technology: Nature study), p. 73–75; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Identify water pollution and stay away from practices that cause it.
activities.prompt_en: When people throw rubbish and oil in the river, the fish die. Let us keep our rivers clean.
steps_en: Show a jar of clean water and a jar with rubbish and oil drops.
Ask: where would a fish like to live?
Talk about where rubbish should go.
Make a poster: “Rubbish in the bin, not in the river!”
observe_en: Chooses the clean water for fish.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 46 (Environmental Education: Pollution), p. 79; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Know that some illnesses come from dirty water and how to stay healthy.
activities.prompt_en: Dirty water can give diarrhoea or cholera. We drink clean water and wash our hands.
steps_en: Show clean water and muddy water.
Ask: which one can we drink?
Say: drink boiled or treated water; wash hands with soap.
If you are sick, tell an adult.
observe_en: Says they will tell an adult when sick.
materials_en: muddy water in a closed jar
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 48 (Health Education and Nutrition: Treatment), p. 81; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Kind to animals and to people
activities.goal_en: Show love, respect and empathy to animals and people.
activities.prompt_en: We are kind to animals: we do not throw stones at them. And we are kind to every friend, even when they are different.
steps_en: Tell a short story of a child who protects a kitten.
Ask how the kitten felt.
Talk about friends who are different (who cannot walk well, who speak another language).
Say kind words to a friend.
observe_en: Says one kind act for animals.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 45 (Character Education: Good behaviour), p. 78; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Use natural painting materials to stamp a pattern.
activities.prompt_en: Leaves, flowers and avocado seeds can make colours. Let us print animal tracks!
steps_en: Prepare natural colours (crushed leaves, flowers, coloured earth) or washable paint.
Dip a stick, a leaf or a cork in the colour.
Stamp a pattern of tracks on paper.
Describe the pattern.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 51 (Painting: Painting materials), p. 84; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Run a relay with animal movements: jumping like a frog, sliding like a snake.
activities.prompt_en: Jump like a frog to the line, slide back like a snake, then touch your friend’s hand!
steps_en: Make two teams.
Show the movements: frog jumps, snake slide on the grass.
Each child goes and comes back, then touches the next friend.
Cheer for both teams.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 53 (Physical Education and Sports: Athletics), p. 86; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

scale.description: Succeeds mostly with a model or help.
Sometimes succeeds alone, sometimes with a reminder.
Succeeds on their own in a familiar situation.

indicators: Makes animal sounds in a story.
Writes c, a, d, e, g, o correctly.
Sorts animals into sets and subsets.
Names farm animals and what they give.
Observes and names birds and insects.
Says why rivers must stay clean.
Prints a pattern with natural paint.

sources: Cameroon Nursery School Curriculum, English Subsystem, MINEDUB, 2018: table 13 (integrated learning themes), p. 37; Nursery Two tables, cited and not reproduced.
